catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Non-agentic structural and domain patterns extracted from the CAS Runner codebase, focusing on governance models, service layers, LLM client abstraction, bootstrap/workspace management, and CI workflow validation.
analysis_limits: Analysis is based on the provided directory tree and key file symbol listings, not a full recursive source read.
Runtime behavior and historical evolution were not observed.
Some interfaces (e.g., an explicit LLM client protocol) are inferred from parallel implementations.
Nested vendored subdirectories (cas-brain, cas-knowledge) were not fully traversed.

system_map.overview: The repository is a Python CLI runner for a Continuous Architecture System (CAS). It provides governance and compliance tooling around architecture knowledge, with a modular package layout under src/cas_runner. The system is organized as a layered command-line application: CLI entrypoint, orchestration runner, service/engine layer, domain models, and infrastructure adapters (LLM clients, bootstrap/file merging). Knowledge is stored on disk in a templated, convention-based directory structure under cas-knowledge.

orchestration.description: The CLI entrypoint (main) invokes FlowRunner, which coordinates governance checks and actions. GovernanceActionService is the facade for transition-driven governance actions backed by GovernanceActionEngine and the TransitionRegistry. ComplianceEngine produces structured findings that feed governance inventory and health models. Bootstrap initializes the workspace by merging governance blocks and creating symlinks/copies for dotfile compatibility. LLM clients are used in skill evaluation and other flows through a swappable adapter layer.

patterns.name: Pydantic Governance Domain Models
patterns.summary: Governance inventory, health, compliance findings, and risk artifacts are represented as typed Pydantic models.
patterns.intent: Ensure governance data passed between compliance checks, health calculations and action engines is validated and self-describing.
patterns.context: The runner executes governance workflows that produce inventories, compliance findings, metrics, and risks; these artifacts must be stable, serializable, and comparable across runs.
forces: Need for schema validation
Need to persist and compare governance snapshots
Avoid loose dictionaries and ad-hoc tuples
patterns.solution: Use Pydantic BaseModel and Enum types to model governance concepts; nested models capture metrics and risk lists; models live in a dedicated governance.models module.
implementation_signals: Classes named GovernanceInventory, GovernanceHealth, ComplianceFinding, GovernanceAction
Nested metrics types such as GovernanceThroughput and TraceableMetric

evidence.note: All governance domain artifacts are declared as Pydantic models.

benefits: Validation on construction eliminates malformed data early
Clear serialization contract for persistence and APIs
Facilitates unit testing of governance logic
costs: Requires schema versioning as governance concepts evolve
Adds Pydantic as a hard dependency in the domain layer
failure_modes: Overly strict models can reject valid legacy data
Model drift from templates and knowledge files if not kept in sync

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: GovernanceActionEngine uses a TransitionRegistry to define valid state transitions instead of scattering conditional logic.
patterns.intent: Make governance action state changes explicit, auditable, and extensible.
patterns.context: Governance actions can transition through a set of states; the engine must know which transitions are legal before applying an action.
forces: Avoid 'if/else' sprawl
Need a central list of allowed transitions
Make new actions easy to add without changing core engine logic
patterns.solution: Create a TransitionRegistry that stores permitted transitions and let GovernanceActionEngine consult it before executing an action.
implementation_signals: Engine logic looks up transitions rather than embedding conditional chains

evidence.note: The transition registry is a first-class construct in the governance action engine module.

benefits: Centralized transition rules are easy to review
New transitions can be added by extending the registry
Supports audit logging by making transitions explicit
costs: Registry must be kept in sync with actual domain state
May require additional indirection for complex guards
failure_modes: Incomplete registry can block legitimate actions
Overly broad transitions can weaken governance

patterns.name: LLM Client Strategy/Adapter
patterns.summary: The system provides interchangeable LiteLLM and mock LLM clients, allowing callers to switch between real and deterministic behavior.
patterns.intent: Isolate the dependency on external LLM providers and enable deterministic tests and local development.
patterns.context: The CLI runner needs to invoke LLM calls for various flows, but should not hard-wire a particular vendor or require network access for all executions.
forces: External LLM APIs are volatile and occasionally unavailable
Tests need deterministic, reproducible responses
Callers should not depend on provider-specific details
patterns.solution: Define a common client interface (implicitly honored by both classes) and provide LiteLLMClient for production and MockLLMClient for test/local use.
implementation_signals: Two client classes in the same llm package with similar method signatures
MockLLMClient returns canned responses without network calls

benefits: Provider changes are localized
Test suite does not require live API access
Can add more providers without touching orchestration
costs: Requires a common interface to avoid duplication
Potential object mapping overhead between provider responses and internal schemas
failure_modes: If the interface is not explicit, clients may drift
Mock responses can become stale compared with real API behavior

patterns.name: Governance Service Layer Facade
patterns.summary: GovernanceActionService acts as a facade over GovernanceActionEngine and its transition registry, exposing higher-level operations to callers.
patterns.intent: Separate orchestration of governance actions from the underlying engine logic and domain models.
patterns.context: FlowRunner and other components need to trigger governance actions, but should not deal with engine internals or transition validation details.
forces: Need to keep the orchestration layer thin
Engine complexity should be hidden behind a stable API
Services should be independently testable
patterns.solution: Implement GovernanceActionService as a service-layer component that wraps GovernanceActionEngine, provides a clean API, and marshals domain models.
implementation_signals: Service methods return governance action results without exposing engine internals

benefits: Reduces coupling between orchestration and domain rules
Easier to mock service behavior in tests
Central place for logging, validation, and error handling
costs: Adds an extra indirection layer
Service API must be maintained as engine evolves
failure_modes: Service can become a god object if all logic is placed there
Facade may hide important engine parameters

patterns.name: Compliance Engine Findings Pipeline
patterns.summary: ComplianceEngine evaluates rules and returns a structured set of compliance findings and metrics.
patterns.intent: Centralize compliance evaluation and produce consistent, queryable results.
patterns.context: The runner must check repository and governance state against multiple rules, reporting success or failure in a uniform format.
forces: Rules may be added or changed independently
Consumers need both aggregate metrics and individual findings
Avoid scattered ad-hoc checks yielding heterogeneous outputs
patterns.solution: Have ComplianceEngine run all checks, collect ComplianceFinding objects, and roll up ComplianceMetrics for reporting.

evidence.note: Compliance engine is the entry point for rule evaluation.
Typed output structures for compliance findings.

benefits: Uniform reporting across rules
Metrics can be used for dashboards and health scores
New rules can be added without changing consumers
costs: Requires all rules to fit the finding model
Complex rules may need extra context that the engine must supply
failure_modes: Finding model can become overloaded with optional fields
Rules may silently degrade if they catch broad exceptions

patterns.name: Pure Health Calculation Model
patterns.summary: Health status and reasoning are computed by pure functions in a dedicated health_model module, separated from dashboard IO.
patterns.intent: Keep health evaluation logic deterministic and testable independently of UI or persistence concerns.
patterns.context: The dashboard needs to show health status and reasons; the underlying calculation should not be tangled with rendering.
forces: Health calculation is reused across CLI and dashboard
Logic must be testable without rendering
Avoid side-effects in the calculation path
patterns.solution: Implement calculate_health and get_health_reasons as pure functions that take data and return a HealthStatus plus reasons.

evidence.note: Calculation functions are separate from any dashboard view.

benefits: High testability
Simple to reason about
Can be reused in different presentation layers
costs: Requires callers to pass all relevant data in
May need additional context if health depends on historical data
failure_modes: If inputs are not well-defined, function can be misused
Too many optional inputs can erode the pure function design

patterns.name: Idempotent Workspace Bootstrap with Merging
patterns.summary: Bootstrap initialization merges governance blocks into dotfiles and creates symlinks or copies, setting up the workspace without destroying user changes.
patterns.intent: Provide a repeatable initialization routine that works across fresh clones and existing workspaces.
patterns.context: The CAS runner needs to install or update .agents and .claude settings, manage governance blocks, and create directory structures.
forces: Different environments may have existing files
Files may be duplicated for compatibility with multiple AI agents
Operations should be safe to run multiple times
patterns.solution: Implement bootstrap with merge functions for governance and Claude settings, and use symlink-or-copy helpers to create required links.

evidence.note: Bootstrap orchestration and file handling are localized.

benefits: Idempotent initialization reduces setup errors
Merging preserves user customizations
Symlink strategy avoids file duplication where possible
costs: Merging logic must understand file formats
Symlink vs copy semantics can differ across platforms
failure_modes: If merge is too aggressive, user edits could be overwritten
Broken symlinks can go unnoticed if not checked

patterns.name: CI Workflow Static Validation Script
patterns.summary: A dedicated Python script statically validates CI/CD workflow YAML files against project-specific rules.
patterns.intent: Enforce CI/CD hygiene (no hardcoded values, pinned installers, reachable dry-runs, active triggers) as code.
patterns.context: The repository has multiple GitHub Actions workflows; manual review is insufficient to catch regressions.
forces: Workflow files are YAML and can contain subtle mistakes
Need to prevent non-compliant workflow changes
Validation should be executable in a pull-request check
patterns.solution: Write a validate_workflows.py script that checks each workflow YAML for syntax, hardcoded values, unpinned installers, unreachable dry-run steps, retired workflows, and correct triggers.
implementation_signals: Other check_* functions targeted at workflow constraints

evidence.note: Validation logic is consolidated in a standalone script.

benefits: Enforces governance rules in CI
Provides quick, localized feedback
Can be extended with new checks
costs: Script must stay in sync with workflow best practices
May duplicate or diverge from actionlint if both are used
failure_modes: Overly strict checks can block valid workflows
Checks might ignore non-GitHub workflow formats

patterns.name: Knowledge Base Convention Directory
patterns.summary: Architecture knowledge is organized into a fixed directory skeleton (global, projects, runtime, templates) with markdown templates for consistent artifact creation.
patterns.intent: Create a discoverable, convention-over-configuration layout for long-lived architecture artifacts.
patterns.context: The CAS uses a knowledge base to store decisions, patterns, rules, maps, and signals across global and project scopes.
forces: Need to locate artifacts quickly
Different artifact types require different metadata
Projects should reuse global patterns and rules
patterns.solution: Predefine directories and markdown templates (e.g., ADR, pattern, rule) so contributors create artifacts in a standard format.
implementation_signals: cas-knowledge/global/decisions, governance, maps, models, narratives, patterns, rules, signals
Template files with names like architecture_decision_record_template.md and pattern_template.md

evidence.note: Pattern template guides the content format.

benefits: Reduces decision fatigue for contributors
Enables tooling to scan and index knowledge
Projects can inherit global governance
costs: Requires discipline to follow the convention
Migration needed when layout evolves
failure_modes: Stale templates can produce inconsistent artifacts
Empty placeholder folders can confuse newcomers

patterns.name: Skill Evaluation Typed Report Models
patterns.summary: Skill evaluation suites and results are modeled as typed Pydantic enums and reports, enabling automated validation.
patterns.intent: Represent evaluation cases, assertions, and results in a consistent, comparable format.
patterns.context: The runner can evaluate skills against test cases, producing a report that can be aggregated and compared over time.
forces: Evaluations need to be machine-checkable
Results should be serializable for storage and comparison
New assertions and statuses should be easy to add
patterns.solution: Define SkillEvalCase, SkillEvalSuite, SkillEvalResult, and SkillEvalReport as Pydantic models with enums for status and assertions.

evidence.note: All eval-related models are grouped in a single module.

benefits: Enforces a consistent contract between eval runner and results
Allows automated quality gates
Easy to persist and read back results
costs: Model changes can invalidate existing reports
Requires careful naming to avoid ambiguous assertions
failure_modes: Too many optional fields may dilute the model
Enum values can become stale as skills evolve

patterns.name: File-System Backed Runtime State
patterns.summary: Runtime state such as traces and evaluations is persisted as files under a dedicated runtime directory.
patterns.intent: Provide an inspectable, auditable record of execution without needing an external database.
patterns.context: The CAS needs to record execution context, traces, and evaluations for later review and governance reporting.
forces: State should be human-readable
Git-trackable artifacts support review
Avoid external infrastructure for a CLI tool
patterns.solution: Store runtime state in a conventional runtime directory (e.g., cas-knowledge/runtime) with subdirectories for traces and evaluations.
implementation_signals: Execution-profile.yaml and rule-context.json are stored in runtime

evidence.note: Trace files are stored on disk.

benefits: Simple to inspect and debug
Leverages existing version control and backup
No external service dependencies
costs: File I/O can become a bottleneck for high-frequency trace logging
Concurrent writes need careful handling
failure_modes: Large traces can bloat the repository
Directory permissions can cause runtime failures

anti_patterns.name: Multi-Agent Dotfile Duplication
symptoms: Same skill names appear under .agents/skills and .claude/skills
Verifier agent definitions exist in both .agents/subagents and .claude/agents
Identical-looking markdown files are maintained in two locations
impact: Updates must be applied in multiple places, increasing maintenance cost
Drift can cause different behavior depending on which AI tool reads the files
Repository becomes cluttered with redundant content
suggested_remediation: Establish a single source of truth and generate or symlink the other variants during bootstrap
Add a validation step to compare the duplicates and fail if they diverge
Document which files are intentionally duplicated and why

anti_patterns.name: Nested Vendored GitHub Directories
symptoms: cas-brain/.github and cas-knowledge/.github contain their own workflow directories
Top-level .github also contains workflows, creating multiple workflow roots
impact: Ambiguity about which workflows are active for the repository
CI behavior can be duplicated or inconsistent if nested subdirectories are not excluded
suggested_remediation: Clearly define whether nested .github directories are vendored or intended to be active
Use explicit ignore/exclude rules in CI and file-walking scripts
Move vendored workflows under a non-`.github` directory if they are not meant to be executed

anti_patterns.name: Implicit LLM Client Interface
symptoms: Two client implementations are present but no explicit Protocol or ABC is visible in the key file snapshot
Callers may depend on concrete implementation classes rather than a stable abstraction
impact: Adapters can silently diverge in method signatures
Adding a third provider requires touching call sites
Testing with mock may not reflect real API behavior
suggested_remediation: Introduce an explicit Protocol (e.g., LLMClientProtocol) in the llm package
Annotate callers with the protocol type to enforce interface compliance
Add a smoke test that verifies both implementations satisfy the protocol
